text:
oliver: Heads up — saw a cluster of invoices with unexpected token spikes for a handful of customers this morning. looks correlated with model-alias -> fallback to quantized variants that rolled in at 03:40 UTC.

oliver: Example: customer A had +18% tokens month-over-month but usage graph shows same request rate. billing preview shows more tokens consumed per request.

mika: huh. any evidence it's tokenization change vs double-counting in the event stream?

oliver: logs show meter events were emitted once, but downstream enrichment applied a different route tag when the fallback fired. eventual invoice aggr grouped by route tag, so those requests got slotted into the reserved-pool bucket instead of hosted, which affected unit price and also triggered invoice adjustments.

sam: can you paste the raw event snippet?

oliver: sure — sanitized snippet:
```
{"event_id":"evt_01Fxxxxx","client_id":"acct_9876","route":"model-alias:chat-medium","model":"redwood/chat-medium@v3","tokens":182,"variant_tag":"fallback:quant-4bit","route_tag":"reserved-pool:eu-west"}
```

oliver: enrichment service later rewrote route_tag to reserved-pool because of routing policy reconciliation. the meterer already consumed the event with route=hosted, but the reconciliation produced a second envelope for accounting. looks like a stale dedupe key for event_id + route_tag mismatch.

jia: billing-bot shows a related invoice adjustment: "2026-03-18 adj: duplicate attribution to reserved pool" — we need to confirm whether invoices were double-billed or just reattributed.

billing-bot: Generated invoice preview for acct_9876 at 2026-03-18 04:12 UTC: base tokens 1,234,567; adjustments +221,304 (route reassignments).

mika: if meterer consumed before reconciliation, why would we get duplicates? we dedupe on event_id at ingest, don't we?

oliver: yes dedupe is event_id only. but the downstream aggregation key is event_id + route_tag to join to route-aware pricing. reconciliation service emits a matching event with same event_id but different route_tag to correct routing later. aggregator treats them as separate keys during the hourly window.

sam: so the root cause is our dedupe scope mismatch. quick wins: 1) expand dedupe key to include normalized-route-affinity in the ingest pipeline, or 2) change reconciliation to emit a delta event instead of a full reemit.

tess: both are invasive. expanding dedupe key will block legitimate reassignments (we sometimes intentionally change route for pricing reasons). emitting deltas reduces event volume but requires aggregator to apply +/-. which is easier to roll back?

jia: UX/ops also: customers saw invoice preview changes with no obvious action. need console flag explaining "route reconciliation in progress" — otherwise support tickets skyrocket.

mika: technical tradeoffs: if we include route_affinity in dedupe, any late reconciliation will be considered a new event and cause attribution drift until backfilled. If we keep current dedupe and switch reconciliation to 'patch' events (op: replace-route) aggregator must understand patch semantics. aggregator currently assumes full-stateless idempotent events.

sam: alt approach: keep current stream but add an enrichment window that holds events for 30s to allow reconciliation to finish, then emit final events. small latency cost but could greatly reduce reassignments.

oliver: agreed — a short buffer might solve most cases because reconciliation usually completes within 10–20s. but we have to be careful with SLOs for real-time previews. console depends on hourly snapshots though, so 30s buffer is probably fine.

tess: two operational concerns: 1) holding adds memory/ops complexity and increases chance of data loss on crashes, 2) which customers do we apply to — all, or only tenants with alias-based routing?

sam: we can try targeted buffering: if event.route_source == "alias-routing" or variant_tag startswith "fallback:" then buffer. low blast radius.

mika: also add a reconciliation flag to events: "recon_expected":true so aggregator can mark a soft-hold. then when reconciliation arrives, we can merge rather than double-count.

jia: support playbook: add console banner and auto-created support tickets for accounts with >5% invoice diff after rollouts. that gives CS heads-up and reduces manual triage.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout of alias-routing-v2 finished at 03:42 UTC (20% traffic). rollback triggered at 04:08 UTC for eu-west reserved-pool traffic.

oliver: rollback explains timing. some late reconciliation messages arrived after rollback and caused the mismatch cluster between 03:40–04:15.

sam: plan proposal (short term): 1) add targeted 30s buffer for alias-routing/fallback events (ingest side) 2) emit reconciliation as delta (op: route_update) — aggregator support behind a feature flag 3) console banner + CS alerting 4) run backfill job to dedupe and reassign invoices for affected accounts.

tess: +1 for targeted buffer. we should also throttle reconciliation re-emits to avoid thrash (exponential backoff if repeated flips).

mika: for backfill, we'll need a deterministic merge function: prefer the last-seen route within canonical window, and compute token attribution delta = tokens * (new_price - old_price). ledger team ok with that?

jia: ledger ok as long as we mark adjustments with reason="route-reconciliation-backfill" and include operator id. CS needs a CSV export for affected accounts.

oliver: I'll open a proposal PR with schema changes (add recon_expected, variant_tag, route_source) and an ingest buffer PoC. assign to eng-platform + billing + console.

sam: I'll owner the aggregator delta support RFC. mika can you scope backfill job?

mika: yep will estimate today.

tess: tagging: @billing, @console, @cs — heads-up. :warning:

oliver: thanks everyone. follow-ups: PR link coming, and I'll post a quick graph in #monitoring when we have before/after.

billing-bot: Created ticket BLG-537: invoice-deltas-route-recon (priority: high).
